column1: # Phase B round ledger — which axis each round advanced.
# Why this file exists (R1526). `tools/phase_b_tally.py` measures an axis by
# COUNTING artifacts, so it can only register work that CREATES one. Depth work
# modifies what already exists: R1523, R1524 and R1525 each closed a named gap
# in the Model/View contract by editing `hello-grid-*` examples the axis already
# owned, and the axis's evidence moved by +0%, +0%, +0%. R1520 and R1521 had
# done the same to the performance axis two rounds earlier. R1522 fixed that one
# by giving perf a `demo-body` probe, which worked only because an optimisation
# happens to leave a NEW demo behind — the cardinality blindness underneath was
# untouched, and it resurfaced on the next axis three rounds later.
# R1522 also recorded why the tool cannot infer this: "a demo is named for the
# round it served and EVERY round has one whatever axis it advanced, so which
# axis owns this demo is frequently unanswerable". Unanswerable BY INFERENCE.
# The round knows. So the round declares it here, and the tally counts
# declarations instead of guessing — the same move as [[r1499]] decoration,
# [[r1501]] surface domain and [[r1517]] focus source.
# Measured before choosing this shape: attributing rounds to axes from git paths
# instead was tried and rejected. R1511 (declared border) and R1513 (dead focus
# half) each touched ~40 examples spanning six axes, so path inference registers
# a sweep round on every axis at once — and unlike a stable false positive in a
# COUNT, which cancels between snapshot and today, that noise ACCUMULATES in a
# rate. Total example bytes was tried too and rejected: it makes verbosity read
# as progress, which the R661 LOC baseline exists to prevent.
# A declaration can be forgotten, which would be the fatal direction (R1522:
# "a false negative on new work is fatal, a false positive cancels"). So git —
# not this file — enumerates which rounds exist, and a round with no row here is
# reported as UNDECLARED at every push. Forgetting is visible, not silent.
# `none` is a legal declaration and needs a reason, for the same reason
# NOT_PHASE_B entries carry one: a documented exclusion can be argued with, a
# silent one cannot.
# Rounds at or below R1519 cannot be declared — the tally was born in R1519 and
# assigning axes to the 1500 rounds before it would be inventing history rather
# than recording it. The floor is stated in the tool and printed in the report.
# Format: round<TAB>axis<TAB>note. Axis is a key from AXES, or `none`.
# round

DisplayTopology plus scene/displays make the desk data, a window position measured from a named display survives the desk changing, and the substitution when that display is gone is named on the wire

a node can BE a graph: the node-system MECHANISM moves out of a 9,000-line example into pinion-node-graph, with the taxonomy left to the application. Re-usable group definitions whose interface is DERIVED from the selection boundary, instances that do not share a value, nesting that cannot recurse, an edit path that prunes, and a collapse refused by reachability where Blender tests a one-hop approximation

a fragment of a graph is a value: Fragment carries the copied nodes, the closure of definitions they instance and the boundary they were cut from, so copy/paste/duplicate/fork are call sites of extract+insert

the push gate learns that a run absent and a run green are different facts: check_base_ci_coverage asks whether the commit being pushed onto has a run of its own, plus a census correction of three debt files whose own bodies said CLOSED while their status field said open. Process round, no Phase B axis advanced

the demo harness is tested past its teardown: 22 cases over request id-matching and the R1552 notification split, wait_until where zero-flake is enforced, the scene readers, key argument rules and the boot gate. Process round, no Phase B axis advanced

a keyboard focus stop is a node in the AT tree: eleven stops across nine bindings had none, so AccessTreeBuilder folded focus onto the window root and a screen reader announced the window. Accessibility repair rather than a Phase B capability advance

the gate computes which packages a change can break instead of remembering the rule: blast_radius.py plus a consumer-test gate in both hooks, with a cap chosen by measurement. Process round, no Phase B axis advanced

the access wire reports the focus THIS window resolves: the shell focus tag is global and AccessTreeBuilder folds it onto the window root, and scene/access republished it into every window. Corrects R1581 own debt registration, whose title was false. Process round, no Phase B axis advanced

a group boundary is a partition and the partition MOVES: group_insert and group_separate change which side of a group a node is on and re-derive the interface from the partition that results, reconnecting every value whose crossing disappeared where Blender reconnects none, re-using a port for a value that already crosses where Blender adds a second, and naming the instances a shared definition dragged along where Blender changes them silently

a method says how a window is named to it: rpc/methods publishes each method window class plus a WINDOW_DOC legend, the class PROVEN by probing all 108 methods rather than parsed (a call graph keyed by function name merges four fn parse and credits two methods with a prefix neither reads), and a window prefix worn on a method NAME is corrected from the catalog instead of meeting a bare -32601 -- the exact call that made R1581 register a false debt. Also carries scene/waitFor refusal cause instead of its wrapper. R1585.1 then gated the probe's OWN population against a params.get census -- the hand-kept superset had eleven names where the surface reads thirty, two of the missing ones path-shaped, so the gate built to prevent a curated population had one

a node says how it takes part and only one of those facts is the graph meaning: bypass takes a node out of the meaning without taking it out of the graph, the routing DERIVED as "the identity as far as the signature allows" where Blender scores a static socket-type table and breaks ties by whether an input happens to be WIRED (so unplugging one port re-routes another), an output no input can feed is NAMED where node_internal_relink deletes the downstream link and returns void, the derivation is read rather than materialised into node runtime internal_links with a pass to notice staleness, dissolve and detach apply the same derivation to the structure, a muted LINK is a different word from a bypassed NODE because they are opposite behaviours Blender spells alike, and Appearance is a separate TYPE from the meaning where Blender keeps NODE_COLLAPSED NODE_PREVIEW NODE_SELECT and NODE_MUTED in one flag integer

a port says whether a value passes through it: Port::no_passthrough is the whole extension point for the bypass routing, read from both ends (an excluded input is never a source, an excluded output receives nothing). CHOSEN BY CENSUS rather than by the debt note that asked for it -- eleven Blender node types register the per-node internally_linked_input callback and their bodies compute exactly three things (the identity by name 7, the identity by index 1, skip the leading control input 3), every one of which this default already produces, while the residue is exclusion, which Blender declares per port (no_mute_links, set through a builder spelled no_muted_links) in 42 places across 17 node files, 28 on outputs and 14 on inputs -- both ends, the shape shipped here. R1587.1 corrected this row: the first census grepped the field name and so found none of the users. So the reference needs eleven C callbacks to reach what is here the default, and the only irreducible residue is exclusion: a control input sharing its data type, and menu_switch nullptr for outputs after the first. The census is held as a TABLE the tests assert against, counts included, after a first draft of it invented a twelfth implementor

the two focus sweeps census ONE derived population instead of one curated list and one derived one: tools/binding_focus.py owns the derivation, both demos import it, and it has its own tests in pre-push. R1518 goes from 14 hand-picked composites to the derived 92, five times the assertions, and the widened census answers what the debt asked and could not measure -- ZERO new focus-stop absences, the five observations it did surface all being bearers in ANOTHER window, told apart from real absences by the resolved field R1583 published and this is the first gate to read. Process round, no Phase B axis advanced

a node can belong to a frame, and belonging is a FOREST: NodeBody::Frame plus Node::parent give the crate the canvas containment it had no concept of (the largest of the eleven Blender census gaps, eight operators), with the invariant checked where Blender states both of its rules as BLI_assert -- and its own NODE_OT_parent_set detaches BEFORE it attaches, so the cycle guard cannot fire even in a debug build. One derivation (Document::outermost) is what enframe, unframe and a drag all act on, where Blender writes it three times over two structs with identical fields. Past Blender: the refusal names the chain, deleting a frame hands its members to the frame ABOVE rather than to the canvas, a duplicate lands back inside its fence where node_copy_local silently detaches, a frame id is not a name so a paste elsewhere joins nothing, an inline keeps the definition's own frames where node_group.cc overwrites every copied node's parent, and the forest is enumerable in one read. It also fixes a pre-existing defect it would have inherited: partition::move_nodes copied the LABEL alone, three rounds after adopt_from was added to make exactly that impossible, so a node crossing a group boundary arrived un-bypassed and un-collapsed

a selection grows by asking the graph a QUESTION, and the answer says what it added: Document::grow closes four of the six operators in the census's selection cluster (linked_to, linked_from, grouped-by-type, grouped-by-prefix/suffix) plus the run under select_same_type_step, as PURE QUERIES -- Blender's set the SELECT bit on bNode and carry OPTYPE_UNDO, so there the question cannot be asked without answering it. Past Blender: the REACH is a parameter where Blender's linked_to/from walk directly_linked_sockets one hop per keypress with nothing saying when the picture stopped changing (added empty is that signal); two instances of DIFFERENT definitions are not one kind where every group node is type_legacy == NODE_GROUP; an affix that is not there offers no criterion where node_select_grouped_name substitutes the WHOLE NAME for a missing suffix; the affix is read off the name that is PAINTED where Blender groups on bNode::name, the datablock id its own header does not draw; and the same-kind RUN is published in evaluation order so an editor can say "3 of 7". The remaining two operators, select_circle and select_lasso, test a region against runtime->draw_bounds and are NOT a node-graph capability -- measured and recorded, with their home named as a region test over tagged scene rectangles

a region of the painted surface is a VALUE: pinion_core::region gives the scene layer the two shapes and the second fit it never had -- Region (rect / circle / lasso) plus RegionFit (intersects / contains), integer geometry, and Scene::hit_test_shape as the general form of hit_test_region. R1590 measured this absence from the node-graph end and recorded that select_circle / select_lasso are NOT node-graph capabilities: they test a region against runtime->draw_bounds, which is a question for the layer that knows what was painted where. Past Qt: three shapes are ONE method rather than three items() overloads; the fit is a per-QUERY argument where QGraphicsView::rubberBandSelectionMode is a view property nothing records per selection; the outcome REPEATS the question; a degenerate lasso is NAMED where items(QPolygonF) answers with the same empty QList an empty surface gets; and the whole thing is askable over a wire, which a QPainterPath cannot be. scene/locate_region gains shape / fit / from, so a lasso select over a real canvas is that method plus the application's own tag mapping. It also fixed the R1585.1 gate itself: its params.get census was a raw substring scan, so every call rustfmt had broken across lines was invisible -- eight params the probe never supplied, `from` among them. Framework substrate round, no Phase B axis advanced

a shape selects in the caller's OWN coordinates: hello-node-editor's marquee, held as four inequalities since R880, becomes the R1591 region predicate -- and the migration found a real defect in R1591's own design, because Region was welded to Rect, an unsigned WINDOW-pixel type, while a node editor selects in graph units that pan negative. Region is now signed throughout with covers_span as its one Rect-free entry point, which is what makes select_lasso and select_circle expressible there at all: two Blender operators become one Region value handed to the one selection policy the pointer marquee uses. It also corrects R1591's own debt note, which named pinion-chart's brush as the second consumer -- measured, that brush is a 1-D RangeSliderExternal x-window with no shape and no hit test, so the note's diagnosis was wrong about half of what it listed. And it closes a coverage hole the counterfactuals found: the marquee's "touching counts" rule, stated in prose since R880, had no test that could fail, because a pointer-driven sweep in screen pixels cannot land on an exact graph-unit edge. Framework substrate round, no Phase B axis advanced

a link may CONVERT: the crate's type relation was symmetric equality (source.ty != sink.ty) and no real node system's is -- a scalar broadcasts into a vector and the vector never narrows back, which is asymmetric, so the crate's own NodeKind doc telling a coercing taxonomy to model it "by making the coercion part of equality" was asking for something no equality relation can be. NodeKind::conversion declares the relation ONCE, as the conversion itself, and that single declaration decides four things the crate spelled as == in four places: whether connect accepts a wire, what arrives along it, which input a bypassed node routes to which output, and whether a document from a file still type-checks. Past Blender 6.x at 8cf50599, which keeps THREE independent answers to that one question and can disagree with itself: validate_link (a bNodeTreeType C function pointer -- and its shader implementation returns true for pairs DataTypeConversions has no entry for), DataTypeConversions (the global Map<(from,to),ConversionFunctions> holding the actual conversion) and get_internal_link_type_priority (a static socket-type table used when a node is muted). Also past it: the crossing is ASKABLE before a wire exists (Document::conversion / link_conversion, where Blender exposes no accessor at all), and showing an implicit conversion costs NO node where Blender materialises a whole implicit_conversion node into the tree. The bypass rule gains its first new clause since R1586 -- the identity as far as the signature allows, and it changes a value only when it has to -- so a direct crossing outranks a converting one at the output's own index, and Route::converts publishes which. The default conversion is equality, so all 151 existing crate tests passed unchanged, which is the backwards-compat proof. Blocks nothing and unblocks the flagship migration: hello-node-editor's PortType lattice (Float broadcasts to Vector, Vector never narrows) was INEXPRESSIBLE on this crate until now, which is the first structural reason debt-two-node-graph-models could not be closed

a socket's value is authored on the NODE: Node::values plus PortRef/Side give the crate what Blender keeps as bNodeSocket::default_value and what the crate had nowhere to put -- a port's TYPE and NAME come from the kind, so every node of a kind shares them, and before this round its VALUE did too. The rule the evaluator applies is ONE SENTENCE COVERING BOTH SIDES: an authored value is what a port carries when nothing else supplies one; for an input that means no link, for an output it means the kind computed nothing there -- which is what makes a SOURCE node's constant this same mechanism instead of a second one. Past Blender 6.x at 8cf50599: a source's constant is a RULE here where Blender's Value node reaches its own output socket's default_value in per-node C code (node_shader_value.cc) that nothing generic shares; authoring is GATED by the signature and refused by name with the arity, where Blender writes a socket's default_value through RNA with no such check; and the value's TYPE is checked through NodeKind::value_type, which Blender gets free from a different C struct per socket type. A value that outlived its port -- reachable by shrinking a definition's interface under an instance that had authored on the port that went away -- is reported as Violation::StrayPortValue. All 161 pre-existing crate tests passed unchanged. The forcing consumer is the proof the mechanism belongs in the crate: hello-node-groups' Op::Swatch([i64;3]) and Op::Level(i64) become UNIT variants, so the taxonomy got SMALLER, and the constant that was unreachable inside it is now editable over the wire (set_value / clear_value / port_values). Second installment of debt-two-node-graph-models: the flagship example's input_defaults and output_const are two ad-hoc fields for this one mechanism

a frame has a HEIGHT: Appearance::height, the last of the three crate gaps that made debt-two-node-graph-models a capability problem rather than a scope one. R1589 recorded the absence and its reason -- an ordinary node's height is a FUNCTION of how many ports it draws, so authoring one would be a second statement free to disagree with the first, while a NodeBody::Frame has no ports and nothing derives its height. Option is what says exactly that. Blender carries bNode::width and bNode::height on every node with no such distinction, and its NODE_OT_resize is horizontal-only for ordinary nodes by convention rather than by anything in the model. Also the round that MEASURED the migration instead of estimating it: parsing main.rs function bodies by brace depth finds 147 of 344 functions (43%) touching the model, over 9,186 lines plus a 9,094-line test file written against its own types -- so a half migration cannot exist, and the eight-step plan is recorded in the debt file for one dedicated session

a cycle NAMES the nodes on it: Document::cycle_nodes, the localisation Violation::Cycle carried no room for, surfaced by the debt-two-node-graph-models migration -- hello-node-editor publishes eval.cycle_nodes and the crate could say only THAT a tree had a cycle, so the flagship consumer would have lost a read on the way in. A node is on a cycle exactly when it is reachable from itself, which is its strongly-connected component having two members or a self-loop of one, and validate now derives both halves from that one walk so "is there a cycle" and "who is on it" cannot disagree. Past Blender 6.x at 8cf50599, which answers the tree-level question with a BOOL (bNodeTreeRuntime::has_available_link_cycle) and localises to LINKS by a heuristic that is not a property of the cycle: update_link_validation clears NODE_LINK_VALID wherever from_node.toposort_left_to_right_index > to_node's, and update_toposort restarts, for a tree with no acyclic start node, "at this node which is somewhere in the middle of a loop" in nodes_by_id order -- so the wire Blender blames moves when only the CREATION ORDER does, which this round holds as a test helper and asserts rather than describes. Iterative Tarjan, not recursion: validate runs on documents that arrived from a file or a peer, and a 4,001-node ring is a test here rather than a stack overflow in the process doing the validating. Also gives TreeId / NodeId / LinkId a Display -- Socket and PortRef already had one, so a consumer building a scene tag or a CSV had to reach through .0, which is the one thing the newtype exists to stop

a frame holds what it was GIVEN: hello-node-editor finishes moving onto pinion-node-graph, closing debt-two-node-graph-models -- the tree carried TWO node models and two frame implementations from R1577 until now, and the example is 9,186 -> 8,331 lines with the duplicate gone. The migration is the round, and what it FOUND is the value: membership was a rectangle re-tested on every read, so widening a comment frame silently adopted nodes and shrinking it abandoned them -- what the frame SAID it held changed with nobody having edited it. It is Node::parent now (R1589, Blender's bNode::parent), and the two gestures that were missing came with it: attach / detach are NODE_OT_attach / NODE_OT_detach, two census operators whose model layer had landed with nothing to reach it, and each ANSWERS the nodes whose frame changed where Blender's operators report only whether the operator ran. Containment reads from both ends and both depths (frame.<id>.contains one level, .contents transitively, node.<id>.parent) where Blender exposes node.parent to Python and has no accessor for a frame's children at all. dissolvable widened from a shape test to LOSSLESSNESS and dissolve_severs.<id> names the wires a dissolve would cut -- node_internal_relink deletes them and returns void, so nothing there can be asked. A cycle can no longer be AUTHORED (connect refuses the closing wire and names the path), and a snapshot undo no longer re-issues an id: Document::advance_ids_from is the crate capability that forced out, because restoring a value restores its mint counters and an agent addressing by id would have been talking about a different node. Also the layout pass itself, lifted (user chose option C over two cheaper ones): pinion-node-graph::layout holds Extent / Layered / Organic / Placement / Quality, because the adapter read exactly four things and only two of them belong to an application -- and lifting it fixed a live defect, a fixed column pitch that charged every column a full card, so a row of reroute knots wasted three quarters of its canvas and a node authored wider than a card overhung the next column. Two crate gaps the migration surfaced and closed: Violation::MistypedPortValue (set_port_value refused a value its port could not hold and validate did not, so such a node evaluated to nothing with no explanation) and Sugiyama::run's determinism stated in its public doc (the projection had inherited a canonicalising sort whose written reason was false -- the solver already guarantees it). Counterfactuals: six, of which CF-3 and CF-4 both PASSED and that is the finding -- the first because no fixture had a cycle, the second because a 3-node 2-cycle is degenerate and decides nothing, so the discriminating shape had to be derived. 251 example tests, 195 crate tests, one RPC demo

a node changes what it IS, not which node it is: Document::set_kind, Blender's NODE_OT_swap_node -- and the shape is the divergence. There the operator CREATES A NEW NODE AND DELETES THE OLD ONE (scripts/startup/bl_operators/node.py, not C++ -- the campaign census had counted it in space_node/*.cc where it appears only as a string in a WM_operatortype_find lookup, the R1587.1 class a third time), so the swapped node's identity dies and every reference to it dies too: a selection, a saved layout, an undo record, an agent holding the id. Here the body changes in place, so the NodeId, the position, the label, the appearance, the bypass and the place in the frame forest all survive. The hard part is that a kind DECLARES its ports (R1594), so changing the kind changes the signature underneath every link and every authored value on the node. One derivation decides what survives -- by NAME, then by POSITION, never against the type relation (R1593's conversion, the same one a link is judged by) -- and it is injective by construction, which is why a swap can neither over-feed an input nor close a cycle and answers no ConnectError at all. Blender picks one of those two rules from a hard-coded pair of node-type sets (transfer_by_index = both_math_nodes or both_switch_nodes, two literal lists in a Python file), so a wire between two kinds nobody put in those lists is dropped even when the ports line up perfectly. PAST BLENDER on reporting too: everything that does not survive is NAMED -- Swapped carries the ports carried (and whether by name), the ports dropped, the links severed and the authored values discarded -- where Blender drops all of it inside three swallowed exceptions (except IndexError, except KeyError, except (AttributeError, KeyError, TypeError)) plus a silent tree.links.remove for a link that turned out invalid, so "the swap worked" and "the swap worked and cost you two wires" are the same outcome there. EditError::NotAKind refuses a frame, a group instance or an interface node by name: a body this crate owns is not the application's to overwrite, and a frame with a signature would be linkable. Counterfactual CF-3 PASSED and that is the finding -- removing the type gate from the NAME pass changed nothing, because the only fixture with an impossible crossing had ports whose names differed, so it exercised the POSITION pass alone; Shout -> Measure is the discriminating shape ("Phrase" matches "Phrase" and crosses, "Out" matches "Out" and Text cannot become Number) and CF-3 then fails. 201 crate tests, 254 example tests, one RPC demo

the graph says WHEN, not only what: a node graph has two kinds of edge and this crate had one. Port::flow (Flow::Value{ty,default} | Flow::Control) is the declaration, and the model change is the method -- the field's TYPE changed rather than gaining a neighbour, so the compiler enumerated all 36 sites that had to decide about control instead of a grep doing it, which is the census failure mode debt-blender-census-by-field-name records four times over. The laws INVERT by flow: a value input takes one producer and a control output takes one successor, one 2x2 derivation (Flow::multiplicity) replacing four hard-coded checks, and a value cycle is a contradiction while a control cycle is a LOOP -- authorable, not a violation, and named statically by Document::control_loops. Document::run derives the execution order from the control plane while data is pulled through the value plane exactly as before, with a stack so a fork runs each arm TO COMPLETION before the next. NodeKind::control is one provided method whose default is a BEHAVIOUR rather than a silence (fall through every control output in port order), which is why a three-way sequence needs no code at all. a graph that REMEMBERS, per instance: NodeBody::Delay plus Machine/tick/settle, and Document::run finally descends into a group instance -- the two halves R1599 named as remaining, and they are one subject because the INSTANCE is the address both need. R1599 made a control loop authorable and recorded why it could not yet mean anything: NodeKind::evaluate is a pure function of the resolved inputs, so a node that ran twice computed the same thing twice. What a second pass needs is a value one step behind -- SSA's phi at a loop header, Lustre's pre, Simulink's Unit Delay -- and this crate owns it rather than the taxonomy for a STRUCTURAL reason an application cannot argue with: evaluate(&self, inputs) has nowhere to put a register, so a taxonomy trying to supply one would have to reach outside itself and one that forgot would have no loops at all. Everything follows from two facts. (1) A delay's output this step is not a function of its input this step, so it CUTS the dependency graph -- which IS Lustre's causality rule ("every cycle must be broken by a pre"), reached here as one predicate (cuts_dependency) that connect, cycle_nodes, data_path_between and validate all read, so they cannot disagree about which cycles are legal; and set_bypassed refuses to bypass a delay a cycle runs through, because a bypassed delay is a plain wire and that is the same illegal state reached by taking the cut away instead of adding the wire. (2) Its register belongs to an INSTANCE, which is the same key the evaluator's memo has used since R1577 -- and that is exactly why control can descend now: entering a group means resolving its interior against THIS instance's inputs, which R1599 recorded as the mechanical blocker (Evaluator's per-instance descent was private and had to be SHARED, not duplicated). Descent is a call stack with a return address per level; a group instance takes no turn of its own, and entering one shows as the first Step inside it, whose Step::instance names it. Simultaneity is enforced by the BORROW CHECKER rather than by convention: tick holds the machine by &mut and the evaluator borrows it immutably, so no register can be written while another is being read -- two mutually-delayed registers therefore swap, where a sequential update gives both the same value (asserted against the rejected design actually running, built from the real evaluator plus Machine::force). Past Blender 6.x at 8cf50599: its Repeat Zone UNROLLS (geometry_nodes_repeat_zone.cc, "the graph is built with as many body copies as there are iterations"), so the count must be known before the graph is built, a data-dependent exit is inexpressible, and memory scales with iterations -- here fifty iterations leave the graph the same size and cost one register; and its simulation state is keyed by a flattened bNestedNodeRef id persisted in the .blend, a side table that must be kept in step with the tree, where the address here is derived by the walk that needs it. Past Unreal 5.8.1: state there is a Blueprint VARIABLE written by an execution wire, so which value a read sees depends on where control went and the graph's meaning is not a function of the graph; and a macro instance is not an instance at all -- FKismetCompilerContext expands one via FEdGraphUtilities::CloneGraph, so N uses are N copies before anything runs, which is why FindMacroCycle has to exist and why its defect matters: it RETURNS on its first macro-instance child instead of continuing the loop, so a cycle reachable only through the second child is never looked for (held as a test helper, asserted to miss a cycle Document::containment finds and names). Counterfactuals: 12, and CF-2 PASSED -- the finding is that every fixture wired its feedback delay-first, where the walk's own cut already answers, so connect's check that the NEW link adds a dependency at all was untested; a consumer-first fixture is now r1600_a_wire_leaving_a_delay_can_never_close_a_cycle. The Machine's wire form was decided by a FAILING TEST rather than by reading the derive: a BTreeMap keyed by (Instance, NodeId) cannot be JSON at all, so registers travel as rows carrying their own address, which is Node's own wire-form argument one level down. 237 crate tests, 10 binding tests, one RPC demo with 44 assertions

the reference census is a TOOL, and it withdrew its own number: tools/reference_census.py plus a pinned judgement (docs/reference-census.json) and a --check-pin gate that needs no reference tree. The campaign's coverage claim rested on a hand grep re-typed each round, and debt-blender-census-by-field-name had already recorded it wrong THREE times in distinct ways (one name two spellings R1587.1, one spelling two meanings R1589, the name is not where the implementation is R1598). Measured: Blender registers node operators FOUR ways -- ot->idname 75, WM_operatortype_append_macro 11, Python core under scripts/startup 27, Python addon 23 -- and the old census saw one, so it MISSED 25 core operators (every Python one, including the entire zone family: add_zone, add_simulation_zone, add_repeat_zone, add_foreach_geometry_element_zone, add_closure_zone, swap_zone, plus six interface_item_* operators) and COUNTED 11 macros, which are compositions of other operators (NODE_OT_translate_attach is TRANSFORM_OT_translate then NODE_OT_attach), as capabilities. Counting a macro as a gap is the false-gap error R1577 already recorded for the 429 registered node types. So 91 was a number whose omissions and false positives happened to cancel: the real figure is 44/56 = 78%, not the claimed 55/59 = 93%, and that claim is withdrawn from CLAUDE.md. It also opened the UNREAL axis, which this campaign had never measured at all: the peer unit is not UK2Node_* (113 of them, content) but FGraphEditorCommandsImpl in GraphEditorActions.h, 78 commands, 20/51 = 39%. Six previously invisible clusters fall out -- alignment 11 (align/distribute/stack/straighten, where pinion-node-graph::layout has only Sugiyama and organic), variadic ports 6 (a kind whose port count is a property of the NODE), struct pins 5, breakpoints 5, watches 2, per-pin type 1. The tool does not JUDGE: coverage lives in the pin, one verdict per operator with a stated reason, and an operator the pin does not judge is reported as a finding rather than counted as either covered or missing -- because a census that silently absorbs a new upstream operator into a percentage is exactly what went wrong. Only have and absent are in the denominator; composition, app-content and addon each leave it with the reason named. --selftest asserts the arithmetic and, pointedly, that a WM_operatortype_find lookup is not read as a registration, which is the R1598 error as an assertion. Also ran the three re-censuses the debt file had listed as unexecuted for a year of rounds and all three prior findings hold exactly: space_node/node_group.cc still contains zero "cycle" mentions, node_group_separate_selected is still the only separate path, and no_muted_links is still 42 call sites across 17 files. Audit-clearance round, no Rust changed

a census verdict is PROVEN BY A TEST: R1601 made the reference census a tool that proves COMPLETENESS -- no upstream operator is silently absorbed into a percentage -- and proves nothing about whether any verdict is TRUE. The 214 judgements were one session's hand reading, and the two error directions are not symmetric: a wrong absent leaves a fake item on the gap list and the next round finds it by trying to close it, while a wrong have INFLATES THE COVERAGE NUMBER AND NOBODY TRIPS OVER IT -- which is the direction R1601 itself had to correct, 93% down to 78%. So every have row now carries proven_by, addressed <crate>::<test>, and 67 proofs land in crates/pinion-node-graph/tests/reference_census.rs (61) and crates/pinion-core/tests/reference_census.rs (3, the region-select trio whose capability R1590 measured as belonging to the painted surface rather than to a node model). Each proof reaches the capability through the PUBLIC API only, which is the position an application is in, and asserts an outcome that would differ if the capability were missing -- measured by isolation, each of four broken mechanisms fails exactly the census proofs that rest on it and no others. The check is in two halves that need each other: reference_census.py --check-pin resolves the address to a census file that exists (a question about paths, so no Rust is parsed and the census-over-text failure this whole tool exists to stop is not reintroduced), and each crate's own census asserts a BIJECTION between the pin rows addressed to it and the proofs it holds. The suspicious verdicts were the COMPOSITION claims -- "call expose again", "there is nothing to sync", "disconnect covers break-node-links" -- because a composition is a hypothesis until it is run, which R1571 already learned by building R1555's written prescription and finding it harmful; all of them hold, and writing them found two facts the pin could not have stated: a Socket names a port INDEX and takes its side from which end of the link it sits on, so break-pin-links must choose an end, and Unreal's hide-no-connection-NO-DEFAULT pins is a filter over the published hidden set crossed with the signature's defaults rather than a second appearance flag. THE SHAPE OF THE BINDING WAS CHOSEN BY A COUNTERFACTUAL: the first draft stored a bare fn() pointer, and CF-2 renaming a proof was NOT CAUGHT, because the bijection compared operator names on both sides and the derived name against the pin, so the function's own identifier was never in the comparison and proven_by was free to name a test that no longer existed. A generic proof() helper reads the name off the function item with type_name_of_val, so the identifier is written once and the string comes from the compiler. 8/8 counterfactuals caught. Closes axis 1 of debt-reference-census-verdicts-are-unreviewed; axis 2 (the Unreal census is one header) stays open and is R1603

the census grows the surface it was BLIND to: a reference does not have one list of things it can do, and reading only one is not incompleteness but blindness -- R1593 (a link may convert) and R1594 (a value is authored on a socket) each closed a prerequisite a node substrate cannot host a material or Blueprint graph without, and both are UEdGraphSchema virtuals in Unreal (CreateAutomaticConversionNodeAndConnections, TrySetDefaultValue) and bNodeType / bNodeTreeType callbacks in Blender, so an OPERATOR census read both as zero and every completion judged on top of it was overstated by exactly the amount nobody could see. tools/reference_census.py now enumerates a second surface on BOTH references -- Blender's bNodeType 20 + bNodeTreeType 7 + bNodeSocketType 7, brace-counted rather than regex-scoped because a struct's extent is a nesting question; Unreal's UEdGraphNode 82 + UEdGraphSchema 115 -- and coverage is reported PER SURFACE, because one denominator would let a fat surface hide a starved one. 231 new rows judged, and the numbers are Blender 54/72 = 75% (operator 78%, hook 62%) and Unreal 60/149 = 40% (command 39%, hook 40%), so R1601's 39% was a lower bound and the widened one lands next to it rather than below. Every have on the new surface is PROVEN: 35 new proofs under R1602's rule, taking the file to 98 tests. THE BIJECTION BECAME A WEAKER RELATION ON PURPOSE, and that is a finding rather than a concession: one pinion mechanism answers SEVERAL reference rows -- Blender's bNodeTreeType::localize and Unreal's UEdGraphSchema::DuplicateGraph are one fork_definition, NODE_OT_delete and SafeDeleteNodeFromGraph are one remove_node -- so a proof now has one OWNER (the row its name derives from) and may be CITED by any number of others, which makes "the reference writes it three times and this derives it once" a machine-readable measurement instead of a sentence R1589 wrote by hand. One new verdict, host-framework, for the 20 rows that are UObject or DNA/RNA lifecycle rather than node-system decisions. The judging rule was stated before it was applied and it follows from R1602's asymmetry: WHEN UNSURE, PREFER absent, because a wrong absent is self-correcting and a wrong have inflates silently. What the new surface NAMES that no operator list could: a kind cannot contribute a rule to Document::validate, a node has no warning state, a port has no description beside its name, there is no per-graph refusal of a node kind, no container socket types, and no relinking of a wire's end. Counterfactuals 5/5 caught, including a surface DROPPED from the census reporting its own rows as GONE rather than shrinking the denominator. Closes axis 2 of debt-reference-census-verdicts-are-unreviewed, and with it the debt
